A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SeTGAP study. Their main text, equations, figures, tables, and complete appendices support reliable comparison, including matching relocated and renumbered content.

before.justification: V2 reports original SeTGAP experiments on synthetic equations, noisy data, SRBench++ functions, and Feynman problems, including repeated-run results and ablations.

after.justification: V3 retains those original experiments and additionally reports runtime measurements and variable-ordering sensitivity results.

M1.justification: The transformer, skeleton generation, recursive merging, MSE-based ordering, and coefficient optimization procedures remain unchanged. Renaming corrVals to MSEVals in Algorithm 1 does not alter the method.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same 13 synthetic problems, noise conditions, four SRBench++ functions, and 78 Feynman problems. The new ordering study selects three existing Feynman cases; the added application examples are motivation, not evaluated domains.

E2.justification: The synthetic comparators remain PySR, TaylorGP, NeSymReS, E2E, uDSR, and TPSR; Feynman comparator membership also remains unchanged. The new Table 5 label NSymRes denotes NeSymReS, whose stated exclusion from E4 and E5 remains.

E3.justification: Appendix K adds comparisons of four variable orderings on each of three Feynman problems, reporting intermediate merge R2 and final-expression metrics. These are additional evaluation configurations; the existing benchmark protocols and default ordering are retained.

E4.justification: V3 adds focused analyses of stage-wise computational cost across the 13 synthetic problems (Appendix H) and ordering sensitivity in three cases with incorrectly identified skeletons (Appendix K). Existing noise tests and hyperparameter ablations remain unchanged.

E5.justification: Repeated-run counts, standard deviation/error reporting, Tukey HSD, and Kruskal–Wallis/Dunn tests with Holm correction are retained. The detailed MSE-testing paragraph moves within the Feynman appendix; the new analyses introduce no additional uncertainty-estimation procedure.

E6.justification: Tables 42 and 51 add runtime and ordering-specific results, including an E4 runtime of 364,147.58 seconds. Existing benchmark values and per-run expressions remain unchanged. New Table 5 adds recovery counts but contains inconsistencies: uDSR E4 is reported as 9/10 although all ten retained per-run tables mark success.

T1.justification: Definition 1, Proposition 1, its Appendix C proof, and the mathematical formulation remain unchanged. The expanded search-space rationale and ordering discussion introduce no new formal theorem, assumption, or derivation.

C1.justification: The abstract and conclusion retain the same contributions and claims about interpretability, functional-form recovery, noise robustness, and competitive Feynman performance. The introduction's clearer post-hoc wording restates the existing explanatory role.

C2.justification: V3 explicitly identifies poor opaque-model approximation as a failure condition and qualifies ordering as a heuristic with problem-dependent effects. It also explains how candidate skeleton structure affects runtime and characterizes the timing measurements as anecdotal.

D1.justification: Appendix H newly discloses an AMD EPYC 7H12 system with 32 physical cores, 30 GB RAM, and no GPU acceleration, alongside component runtimes. It also states that further parallelization of Algorithm 3 has not been implemented. These are additional disclosures about the existing pipeline.

R1.justification: The application motivation adds references to Cranmer et al. (2020), Delgado et al. (2022), Reinbold et al. (2021), KM3NeT Collaboration (2025), and Morales and Sheppard (2026). The main positioning against prior symbolic-regression methods remains unchanged.

P1.justification: Localized rewrites expand application motivation, mechanism explanations, and limitations; terminology changes include corrVals to MSEVals. Appendices H and K are inserted while the main organization remains intact. Section 4.1 also acquires the stray fragment 'functional form.'

P2.justification: V3 adds the recovery-summary, runtime, and ordering tables (5, 42, and 51), reformats the SRBench++ equation table, and relocates several figures and algorithms. Existing figure graphics are unchanged; retained appendix tables are primarily renumbered or relocated.

improvement.justification: V3 supplements v2's qualitative cost warning and untested ordering rationale with concrete diagnostics in Appendices H and K, while clarifying dependence on opaque-model accuracy. This improves transparency and critical evaluation. The gains are limited by anecdotal timings, the three-case ordering study, and inconsistent recovery counts in new Table 5, including uDSR's E4 count.
